question_english: What local Ghanaian foods boost blood count (iron) during pregnancy?
question_twi: Ghana aduane bɛn na ɛma mogya (iron) kɔ soro wɔ nyinsɛn mu?
answer_english: Local foods rich in iron include Kontomire (cocoyam leaves), Turkey berries (Abedru/Kwahu Nsoso), liver, dark leafy greens, and beans. Pair them with oranges or lemons (Vitamin C) for maximum iron absorption.
answer_twi: Aduane a iron wom pii ne Kontomire, Abedru (Kwahu Nsoso), akoma/akuma, ne aboboi/beeni. Di mu ne lemur anaa ankaa nsuo na ama wo nipadua agye iron no pɛpɛɛpɛ.

question_english: What are the early warning signs of pregnancy complications?
question_twi: Nsɛnkyerɛneɛ bɛn na ɛkyerɛ sɛ haw wom wɔ nyinsɛn mu?
answer_english: Key danger signs include vaginal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, persistent high fever, swelling of the face and hands, severe headaches with vision changes, and sudden reduction in fetal movement.
answer_twi: Nsɛnkyerɛneɛ hu ne mogya a ɛfiri wo mu, ayaase yareɛ denden, ho hye denden, anim ne nsa a ɛhonntɛm, tiri yareɛ denden ne ani wusuwusu, ne abofra a wosow a ɛte ase.

question_english: How long should I exclusively breastfeed my newborn baby?
question_twi: Mmerɛ ahe na ɛsɛ sɛ mekyɛ nufoɔ nko ara ma me ba?
answer_english: Ghana Health Service and WHO recommend exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months of life. Do not give water, teas, or infant porridge during these first 6 months unless medically instructed.
answer_twi: GHS ne WHO kyerɛ sɛ ma abofra no nufoɔ nko ara asram mmiensa ne mmiensa (6 months). Mma no nsuo, herbal tea, anaa koko wɔ saa asram 6 mu koraa.

question_english: Can I drink Nibima or Taabea bitters for malaria while pregnant?
question_twi: Metumi anom Nibima anaa Taabea bitters de asa asram (malaria) nyinsɛn mu?
answer_english: Do not self-medicate with herbal bitters for malaria during pregnancy. Always visit the ANC clinic for approved malaria prophylaxis (like SP tablets) and prescription antimalarials tested for fetal safety.
answer_twi: Mma wmma wo ho herbal bitters pii nyinsɛn mu. Kɔ ayarsabea clinic na wɔma wo SP aduru a agye din a ɛbɔ wo ne wo ba ho ban pɛpɛɛpɛ.

question_english: Is it normal for a baby to develop mild fever after immunization?
question_twi: Ɛyɛ krow na abofra ho yɛ hye kakra bere a wanya nsuro wie?
answer_english: Yes, mild fever or soreness at the injection site is a normal sign that the baby's immune system is responding to the vaccine. Give prescribed paracetamol syrup if recommended by the nurse, and keep the infant hydrated.
answer_twi: Aane, ho hye kakra anaa baabi a wɔwɔ no kɔ nsa yɛ abodeɛ mu kyerɛ sɛ abofra no immune system renyin. Ma no paracetamol syrup kakra sɛ nurse no hyɛɛ wo kwan a.
